schema:
CREATE TABLE nodes (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,
    title TEXT NOT NULL,
    body TEXT NOT NULL,
    metadata_json TEXT NOT NULL,
    digest TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
)

CREATE TABLE claims (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES nodes(id),
    payload_json TEXT NOT NULL,
    digest TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
)

matched_rows.title: Open problem: An iid FPP law with proved KPZ exponent relation
matched_rows.body:
OPEN PROBLEM from the Codex campaign ledger (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). Exhibit a nondegenerate iid undirected FPP law with well-defined fluctuation and wandering exponents satisfying chi=2xi-1. Source: Auffinger, Damron and Hanson: 50 years of first-passage percolation, Question22, PDF p.89; equation4.19.
Posed in Auffinger, Damron and Hanson: 50 years of first-passage percolation
Status as recorded in the campaign ledger on 2026-09-07

matched_rows.title: Attempt on An iid FPP law with proved KPZ exponent relation
matched_rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: An iid FPP law with proved KPZ exponent relation structural argument Result: If a geodesic deviates transversely by n^xi and the norm has quadratic curvature, the deterministic excess norm over a displacement of length n has order n*(n^(xi-1))^2=n^(2xi-1). This yields the proposed balance only after assuming random fluctuations are of the same order. Check: The power follows from norm homogeneity and the square of the relative transverse displacement. A curvature exponent kappa would instead give kappa*xi-(kappa-1). Obstruction: Both the required exponent existence and error control when replacing random passage times by the norm remain unproved for a concrete iid law here. The balance calculation is conditional, not a proof.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0110-an-iid-fpp-law-with-proved-kpz-exponent-relation
No independent review
